summary: Imitates real materials so the control explains itself. A perceived affordance, in Don Norman's sense.
source: Wikipedia Skeuomorph (Norman framing) · Looka (iOS 7 / Windows 8 as the break) · LogRocket · Apple iOS 6 / OS X Mountain Lion 2012 · current hardware-UI reference galleries (Justinmind, Dribbble, Design Studio)

chassis.role: the device face — light metal, not beige leather

knob.role: control bodies — dark, so they read against the face

accent.role: the one saturated panel. Takes WHITE at 4.6:1

led.role: a status lamp, not an accent

shadow.rule: always alpha, always soft. Pure #000 at full opacity is banned.

gradient.note: 4 stops with a 4% HARD BREAK at the midpoint — that break is what reads as a moulded surface rather than a fade

light.rule: ONE light direction per screen. This is the single most common failure.

focus.reason: the one screen-native colour this pack permits, and only here. A material focus ring would compete with the bevels; a blue ring reads as a system affordance layered ON the material, which is what it is.

motion.note: a physical control moves when pressed. 60ms — faster than a UI transition, because matter is stiff.

copyBudget.note: labels are engraved into a surface, which caps how much text a control can hold

a11y.note: Norman's 'perceived affordance': the raised look IS the signifier. That makes this pack unusually strong on discoverability and unusually weak on scale — every control must be individually rendered.
a11y.falseAffordanceRule: A raised look on something that is NOT clickable is the pack's cardinal sin. If it looks pressable it must be pressable.
a11y.radiusNote: Raised to 60 because a rotary knob is border-radius:50%. On a 72px knob that resolves to 36px, which is a control geometry rather than a soft-UI decision.
a11y.meterNote: An LED meter reads green/amber/red because that is what a meter does — it is instrumentation, not palette. The hue budget counts it, so the cap is raised to 6 rather than pretending the meter is decorative. The PALETTE is still two-tone chassis plus one accent.

banned: more than one light direction on a screen — the single most common failure
flat solid background on an interactive control
pure #000 shadows at full opacity — always alpha, always soft
a raised look on something that is not clickable (false affordance)
screen-native accent colours like #0af or #f0f — they break the material illusion
icons drawn flat and then dropped onto a textured surface

darkMode.note: A dark material, not an inverted one — walnut and brushed steel rather than beige leather. The light direction stays top-left; inverting it would read as the object being lit from below, which no real object on a desk ever is.

scroll.headline: scroll-snap (●)
scroll.reason: physical controls DETENT — a dial clicks into position, it does not drift. Snap is the only technique in the catalogue that models a real mechanical behaviour rather than an optical one.
banned: text-reveal — type here is printed, engraved or embossed ONTO a material. It cannot fade in, because it is part of the surface

notes.tokens: Don Norman calls this a perceived affordance — a visual detail telling you an action is possible. The modern register for it is hardware: a rotary knob affords grabbing in a way a leather texture never did. Two-tone is the norm — a light chassis carrying dark controls — with one saturated panel and a single light direction, top-left, across the whole device.
notes.nav: A brushed bar with a contact shadow underneath — it sits on the surface rather than floating above it. The active item is recessed, not highlighted: a pressed key stays down.
notes.hero: A device chassis, not a page section: bounded, bevelled, screwed down, with its controls arranged on the face. The 4% hard break at the gradient's midpoint is what reads as a moulded panel rather than a fade.
notes.button: Three shadows at once — bevel highlight, contact, ambient. Pressed swaps all of them for a single inset and moves the control 1px, in 60ms, because matter is stiff. Focus is the one screen-native colour the pack permits.
notes.form: An input is a WELL — recessed, with the light still coming from top-left, so the highlight is on the bottom edge. Getting that backwards is the fastest way to break the illusion.
notes.card: A panel, lifted by contact and ambient shadow together. One light direction: every highlight on this page is top-left and every contact shadow falls bottom-right.
notes.table: Engraved rules on the material. This pack has no honest table vocabulary — real objects do not have data grids — so it borrows a ledger: ruled lines pressed into the surface.
notes.overlay: A dialog that sits above the page on a strong ambient shadow. The scrim is warm, not neutral grey — a neutral scrim would sit outside the material world the rest of the page builds.
notes.empty: A recessed well with nothing in it. This is the pack's most natural empty state: an empty slot is a real thing, and it needs no dashed border to explain itself.
notes.dark: A dark material, not an inverted one — walnut and brushed steel rather than beige leather. The light direction stays top-left; inverting it reads as an object lit from below, which nothing on a desk ever is.
notes.narrow: Bevels and shadows do not scale down: a 1px highlight on a 44px control reads correctly, on a 24px control it disappears. Controls get larger at narrow widths here, not smaller.
notes.copy: Labels are engraved into a surface, which caps how much text a control can hold — hence 2-word buttons.

researchNote: Checked against current reference galleries before rebuilding. The modern register for this style is HARDWARE - audio interfaces, mixing consoles, calculators, instrument panels - not the beige leather-and-linen of iOS 6. The vocabulary is rotary knobs with indicator lines, faders in recessed tracks, toggle switches, LED meters and a bounded device chassis, usually two-tone (light chassis with dark controls) and often carrying one saturated accent panel. That register is also the honest one for Norman's 'perceived affordance': a knob affords grabbing in a way a leather texture does not.
